**Step 1 — Scene:** Scrambled eggs with mixed salad leaves, roasted Brussels sprouts, and a small piece of tomato.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A rounded-square dinner plate, partly cropped. Using an approximate equivalent diameter of **26 cm**, its area is **3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm²**.

**Steps 3–6 — Items, coverage, volume, and weight:**

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × typical height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Scrambled eggs | 30% | 159 cm² × 1.3 cm = 207 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 197 g |
| Mixed salad leaves | 30% | 159 cm² × 2 cm = 318 ml | 0.15 g/ml | 48 g |
| Roasted Brussels sprouts | 7% | 37 cm² × 2 cm = 74 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 48 g |
| Tomato piece | 2% | 11 cm² × 1.3 cm = 14 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 9 g |

Coverage totals **69%**, consistent with the substantial empty plate around the food. A light sheen suggests approximately **4 g of oil/dressing** on the vegetables; this overlaps their area rather than adding coverage.

**Step 7 — Energy:** Eggs at 160 kcal/100 g contribute approximately 315 kcal; leaves at 20 contribute 10 kcal; sprouts at 45 contribute 22 kcal; tomato at 18 contributes 2 kcal; oil at 884 contributes 35 kcal. The egg estimate includes modest cooking fat, while the separate oil estimate applies only to the vegetables.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **306 g and 384 kcal** is plausible for this visible portion. Most of the weight and energy comes from the eggs; the leafy pile is relatively light.
